content.text: In the general discussion channel, Odilitime mentioned that the community had to migrate away from Ai16z, noting it was worth attempting to gain more traction elsewhere. Separately, a hostile exchange occurred between two users, with one making personal and inflammatory remarks toward another member. MDMnvest shared a link to a Ruby Trivia AI event on X, promoting a Thursday night stream at 9 PM where the top 3 players would win 0.1 SOL each with no entry required. Additionally, a user named Ginga posted asking if anyone in the community was looking to hire a developer.

A developer named mackroute announced a new plugin for Eliza agents designed to assess Solana token rug pull and honeypot risk before an agent executes a trade. The plugin returns a signed verdict with a score from 0 to 100 along with machine-readable reasons that can be verified offline. It operates on a pay-per-call model using USDC via x402, allowing agents to settle payments autonomously without requiring an account. A free lookup is available to test the model. The developer posted in the coders channel seeking feedback from developers who are actively running trading agents on Solana, specifically asking whether pre-trade risk checks would be useful or if they already handle risk assessment through other means.

In the partners channel, community members exchanged casual greetings. One member expressed missing the group, which received positive reactions. Another member responded warmly, and a third tagged Shaw in a follow-up reply. Separately, in the general discussion channel, a message was flagged as spam by a community member in response to what appeared to be an airdrop announcement account.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Update: Legal Resolution, Project Status, and Developer Activity

content.text: A major legal milestone was announced on July 9, 2026. Federal Judge Jed S. Rakoff signed a Stipulation and Order of Dismissal on July 8, 2026, formally resolving the case of Pikabea v. Walters et al. The order dismisses the plaintiff's individual claims with prejudice against all defendants, with no costs or attorneys' fees awarded to any party. The proposed class claims were dismissed without prejudice. The court retains jurisdiction for 30 days solely to enforce the settlement agreement. Community members celebrated this as the end of the legal issues surrounding Shaw (Walters) and the broader elizaOS ecosystem, with some expressing optimism that this marks the beginning of a new phase for the project and the $ELIZAOS token.

Despite the positive legal news, some community members raised concerns about the current state of the project. One user noted a lack of public announcements and minimal activity on social media, questioning whether the project was still active. In response, a core community member acknowledged that the marketing staff had been let go, and that the foundation and Shaw remain involved, with cloud described as the current strategic focus. Active community members were identified as the remaining operational presence.

In the coders and discussion channels, several developers posted availability and collaboration offers. One senior AI and full-stack engineer advertised white-label technical partnership services for US agencies, covering AI, backend, automation, and voice-agent projects. Another engineer with AI and ML expertise listed capabilities including RAG systems, AI agents with memory and task automation, voice AI using STT and TTS tools, OCR, visual search, and full-stack SaaS platforms, using tools such as OpenAI, Claude, LangChain, LangGraph, Python, FastAPI, Next.js, and Node.js. Additionally, a separate post in the coders channel sought a non-technical person for a flexible, part-time opportunity.

An event was promoted in the discussion channel for MOI Builders number 5, a builder session focused on combining AI and Web3 development. The session involves using Claude to generate logic and deploying a live application on the MOI platform, walking participants through the process from idea to deployment in a single session. Builder bounties were to be announced live at the event.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Marketing, Token Strategy, and AI Agent Use Cases

content.text: In the general discussion channel, community members discussed the role of the Eliza Foundation, which was clarified to be in charge of the token. A conversation around marketing strategy emerged, with one member suggesting that marketing efforts should be ramped up when market conditions improve. They proposed using a portion of the team's token allocation to fund marketing campaigns, potentially offering community members discounted tokens with a lock period to raise funds. Another member countered that product development and revenue generation should take priority over marketing, noting that a successful product will naturally attract attention and that marketing the brand and development progress is possible in the meantime. Separately, a developer posted that they are looking for work, and another member shared that Ruby Trivia, a crypto-related trivia game, is now live for download on Amazon. A contributor also shared the Zeroclaw open-source project, described as a fast, small, and fully autonomous AI personal assistant infrastructure compatible with any OS and platform, and invited community members to join as beta-testers.

In the coders channel, a developer from Argentina introduced themselves and asked the community to explain practical and intuitive use cases for AI agents beyond the commonly known ones such as planning, code review, and testing. They expressed interest in understanding how others have integrated AI agents into their workflows in meaningful ways. The conversation was just getting started with greetings exchanged among members.

A community member shared that the Ruby Trivia app, tagged under web3, gaming, elizaos, crypto, and memecoin categories, is now officially live on Amazon. The app was announced via a Farcaster post by user Magicyte.

A community member noted that ERC-8004, a standard for agent verification and reputation, was implemented about a month ago. They observed that someone appears to have ported the structure over to Solana in a project called HANKO by hanko-labs, described as a Solana agent trust registry with bond and slash mechanics. The member asked for confirmation from more knowledgeable community members. A bot attempted to analyze the repository but failed. The GitHub repository can be found at https://github.com/hanko-labs/hanko.

In the coders channel, Odilitime briefly commented that certain tools or features can be used for anything, though the specific context of the conversation was not fully captured in the available data.

categories.title: ElizaOS Community Discussion: Token Buybacks, Relaunch Speculation, and Technical Issues

content.text: On July 12, 2026, the ElizaOS Discord discussion channel saw several topics come up among community members. One user raised questions about token buybacks, asking whether there would be public reporting on buyback amounts once they begin, and whether revenue from Milady flows into the buyback pool or remains separate. The user expressed that this kind of transparency would help holders track progress rather than relying on trust alone. Another community member asked where the roadmap could be viewed and was directed to a dedicated channel, with a note referencing the version before the new logo. A separate exchange touched on profitability concerns, with one member simply asking whether there is any profit, receiving no detailed response. Two members speculated that ElizaOS may need a total relaunch starting from a v3 launch, citing too much dead weight currently in the project. On the technical side, a user reported persistent issues with ElizaOS failing with an 'Error generating text' message and always requiring a Groq API key despite using an Eliza Cloud key. The user had attempted rebuilding the repository multiple times using different AI keys including Eliza Cloud, OpenAI, and Groq, and had also tried running through Eliza Cloud directly. The system continued attempting to call the Groq model qwen-qwq-32b and returning an invalid API key error. A moderator suggested clearing the ~/.eliza directory and starting over, while another helper asked how long the issue had been occurring.

In the general discussion channel, a user posted a recruitment-style message advertising various paid roles including Beta Tester at $20/hour, Moderator at $350-400/week, Developer with negotiable rates for Rust, Python, or C++ skills, and Community Manager at $800/week, among others, asking interested parties to send a DM. Separately, a user shared a link to an X post and noted that elizaOS has very few updates on social media but believes the project is worth attention, also mentioning they discovered another project attempting to attract the elizaOS team's attention. Another user posted a lengthy proposal formatted as an AI evaluation request, pitching a nightlife and cultural event concept called Love Train Bronx targeting The Bronx, New York, framing it as an untapped web3 community market opportunity and requesting seed funding or a micro-grant. Odilitime briefly commented on a 0.x plugin appearing in 2026, suggesting some skepticism. General greetings and a shared X post link rounded out the channel activity.

In the coders channel, a developer introduced themselves as building paralens.ai, described as a structured transaction understanding engine for onchain activity. They asked what data sources or APIs agents currently use to understand wallets and transactions, and whether transaction-level intelligence or wallet-level behavioral datasets would be more valuable. Odilitime responded that elizaOS currently supports Helius, Birdeye, CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, and more. The developer followed up asking whether those integrations are sufficient for understanding complex DeFi transactions or if there is custom logic on top for interpreting user actions and behaviors, to which Odilitime replied that there is probably always room for more. Additionally, a software engineer with a background in healthcare, finance, education, SaaS, and game development posted an introduction seeking collaborators for business expansion and long-term partnership, regardless of prior development experience.
